sampling_model.design: A fixed-period observational panel is reweighted to the ex ante absorbing-path law \(\Pi\).
sampling_model.units: The triples \((X_i,W_i,Y_i)\) are independent and identically distributed draws from \(P\), with fixed \(T\).
sampling_model.treatment: The path \(W_i\) takes values in the declared absorbing support \(\mathcal S\).
sampling_model.overlap: The observed generalized propensity obeys \(\pi_s(X)\ge c_{\pi}\), and the reshaping law obeys \(\Pi_s\ge\epsilon\), for every \(s\in\mathcal S\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The core is a population identification and diagnostic result; estimation of \(\pi\) is not part of this specialization.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under a calendar-homogeneous finite-lag outcome model and a nonsingular reshaped design, each dynamic RIPW coefficient converges to the corresponding average lag effect.
A conventional event-study lag coefficient is a weighted average of cohort effects from its own and other relative periods.
Inverse-probability estimators of finite-memory dynamic effects are unbiased under the known panel randomization, with finite-population limit theory.
Under a time-constant random-coefficient distributed-lag model, average lag coefficients can be identified in complex treatment designs.
Conventional staggered event-study regressions admit computable probability-limit diagnostics for negative weights and cross-horizon contamination.
A time-varying parameter distributed-lag model permits lag coefficients to vary with past information.

body.tldr: A reshaped distributed-lag fixed-effect coefficient is characterized as an exact linear functional of calendar-specific current and carryover effects. The loading tensor has both an ordered bridge-kernel formula and a pair-mass formula, its normalization reproduces the published homogeneous dynamic RIPW theorem, and rational inputs admit exact rank and contamination certificates. The unresolved theorem asks for an ordered adjacent-mass rule that classifies every loading sign and every zero off-diagonal entry without solving the exhausted inverse-image problem.

project_justification.gap: Published RIPW theory states consistency of dynamic coefficients under effects that are homogeneous over calendar time and explicitly leaves the time-varying DATE equation beyond scope. Conventional event-study decompositions retain cohort and horizon cells but do not study counterfactual assignment-law reshaping with finite-memory lag regressors.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is the forward coefficient-by-calendar-by-causal-lag tensor under a fixed positive reshaping law, together with a support-only rank test and an ordered sign geometry.
project_justification.fill: The project derives that tensor in pair-mass and Green-kernel coordinates, certifies its exact computation, proves its strict reduction to the homogeneous theorem, and isolates the sign frontier as the open structural problem.

body.related_work: Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo (2024) supply the RIPW design, the DATE equation, and a dynamic consistency theorem under calendar-homogeneous lag effects; Theorem \(3\) makes their result an exact special case and proves strict extension beyond its maintained model. Sun and Abraham (2021) provide the foundational decomposition of conventional event-study coefficients into own-horizon and cross-horizon cohort effects; their residualization logic informs, but is not claimed to be tightened by, the reshaped lag-design tensor. Bojinov, Rambachan, and Shephard (2021) analyze carryover under known experimental assignment and motivate treatment-history indexing; their finite-population estimators are distinct from the present observational reshaping functional. De Chaisemartin and D'Haultfoeuille (2025) analyze complex treatment paths and a random-coefficient distributed-lag model whose effects remain constant over time; their result confirms that calendar variation remains outside the closest distributed-lag recovery framework. Wright (2026) gives conventional staggered-event-study probability-limit diagnostics and orthogonal scores but does not use assignment-law reshaping or a finite-memory calendar-by-lag tensor, so it is treated only as adjacent public-manuscript evidence. Ailigeng, Lu, and Wang (2023) provide published modeling precedent for time-varying distributed-lag coefficients but do not study causal panel reshaping or fixed-effect loading geometry.
body.honest_scope: The forward loading identities, normalization, homogeneous reduction, support-rank certificate, and exact rational diagnostic are theorem obligations. The ordered sign-and-zero rule is genuinely open and is not supplied by the assumptions. The project does not characterize the inverse image of all attainable tensors, optimize over reshaping laws, or claim double-robust inference. When \(p=0\), Theorem \(2\) reduces to the static DATE loading identity of Arkhangelsky, Imbens, Lei, and Luo; when effects are homogeneous over calendar time, Theorem \(3\) reduces to their published dynamic theorem.
